questions.question:
Which one or more of the following CPU scheduling algorithms can potentially
cause starvation?
questions.explanation:
Check whether a process can wait forever:
- FIFO: every process eventually reaches the front [latex]\text{---}[/latex] no starvation.
- Round Robin: each process gets a time slice every round [latex]\text{---}[/latex] no starvation.
- Priority scheduling: a low-priority process may wait forever if high-priority processes keep arriving.
- SJF: a long job may wait forever if short jobs keep arriving.

Answer: Priority Scheduling, Shortest Job First

questions.question:
Three concurrent processes X, Y, and Z execute three different code segments that access and
update certain shared variables. Process X executes the P operation (i.e., wait) on semaphores
a, b and c; process Y executes the P operation on semaphores b, c and d; process Z executes the
P operation on semaphores c, d, and a before entering the respective code segments. After
completing the execution of its code segment, each process invokes the V operation (i.e., signal) on
its three semaphores. All semaphores are binary semaphores initialized to one. Which one of the
following represents a deadlock-free order of invoking the P operations by the processes?

options.A: X: P(a)P(b)P(c) Y: P(b)P(c)P(d) Z: P(c)P(d)P(a)
options.B: X: P(b)P(a)P(c) Y: P(b)P(c)P(d) Z: P(a)P(c)P(d)
options.C: X: P(b)P(a)P(c) Y: P(c)P(b)P(d) Z: P(a)P(c)P(d)
options.D: X: P(a)P(b)P(c) Y: P(c)P(b)P(d) Z: P(c)P(d)P(a)

questions.explanation:
Deadlock is impossible if all processes request semaphores in one common global order.

Option 2: X: b, a, c; Y: b, c, d; Z: a, c, d. All follow the order b [latex]\lt[/latex] a [latex]\lt[/latex] c [latex]\lt[/latex] d, so there is no circular wait.

The other options have conflicting orders (e.g. one process takes b before c and another takes c before b).

Answer: X: P(b)P(a)P(c), Y: P(b)P(c)P(d), Z: P(a)P(c)P(d)

questions.question:
A computer uses 46-bit virtual address, 32-bit physical address, and a three-level paged page table organization. The page table base register stores the base address of the first-level table (T1) ,which occupies exactly one page. Each entry of T1 stores the base address of a page of the second-level table (T2 ) Each entry of T2 stores the base address of a page of the third-level table (T3 ) Each entry of T3 stores a page table entry (PTE). The PTE is 32 bits in size. The processor used in the computer has a 1 MB 16 way set associative virtually indexed physically tagged cache. The cache block size is 64 bytes.

What is the size of a page in KB in this computer?
questions.explanation:
Let page size = [latex]2^p[/latex] bytes. Each table page holds [latex]2^p/4=2^{p-2}[/latex] entries, and T1 fits in one page.

[latex]46=p+3(p-2)\Rightarrow4p=52\Rightarrow p=13[/latex]

Page size = [latex]2^{13}[/latex] = 8 KB

Answer: 8

Page colours needed = [latex]2^3=8[/latex]

questions.question: Consider a CPU that has to execute two types of processes. The first type, Actuators (A), requires a CPU burst of [latex]6[/latex] seconds. The second type, Controllers (C), requires a CPU burst of [latex]8[/latex] seconds. A new process of type A arrives at time [latex]t=10[/latex], [latex]20, 30, 40[/latex], and [latex]50[/latex] (in seconds). Similarly, a new process of type C arrives at time [latex]t=[/latex] [latex]11, 22, 33, 44[/latex], and [latex]55[/latex] (in seconds). The CPU scheduling policy is First Come First Serve (FCFS). The first process of type A starts running at [latex]t=10[/latex] seconds. The average waiting time (in seconds) for the [latex]10[/latex] processes is ________. (rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.explanation:
List all [latex]10[/latex] arrivals in chronological order and simulate FCFS execution (CPU serves strictly in arrival order, non-preemptive):

[latex]\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c}\text{Proc}&\text{Arrival}&\text{Burst}&\text{Start}&\text{Finish}&\text{Waiting}\\\hline A&10&6&10&16&0\\C&11&8&16&24&5\\A&20&6&24&30&4\\C&22&8&30&38&8\\A&30&6&38&44&8\\C&33&8&44&52&11\\A&40&6&52&58&12\\C&44&8&58&66&14\\A&50&6&66&72&16\\C&55&8&72&80&17\end{array}[/latex]

Sum of waiting times [latex]=0+5+4+8+8+11+12+14+16+17=95[/latex].

Average waiting time [latex]=\dfrac{95}{10}=9.5[/latex] seconds.

Answer: 9.5

questions.question:
A certain computation generates two arrays a and b such that a[i]=f(i)for [latex]o\leq i \lt n[/latex] and b[i] = g (a[i] )for [latex]o\leq i \lt n[/latex]. Suppose this computation is decomposed into two concurrent processes X and Y such that X computes the array a and Y computes the array b. The processes employ two binary semaphores R and S, both initialized to zero. The array a is shared by the two processes. The structures of the processes are shown below.

Which one of the following represents the CORRECT implementations of ExitX and EntryY?

Y must not use a[i] before X has produced it, and X must not run ahead.

Y signals S (ready), X waits on S, then signals R after a[i] is written, and Y waits on R. The two stay in step without deadlock.

questions.question: A disk of size [latex] 512M [/latex] bytes is divided into blocks of [latex] 64K [/latex] bytes. A file is stored in the disk using linked allocation. Each data block reserves 4 bytes to store the pointer to the next data block. The link part of the last data block contains a NULL pointer (also of 4 bytes). Suppose a file of [latex] 1M [/latex] bytes needs to be stored in the disk. Assume, [latex] 1K=2^{10}, 1M=2^{20} [/latex]. The amount of space in bytes that will be wasted due to internal fragmentation is _________. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
Disk block size [latex]=64K=2^{16}[/latex] bytes. In linked allocation, every block (including the last) reserves [latex]4[/latex] bytes for its "next" pointer field, leaving usable data capacity per block [latex]=65536-4=65532[/latex] bytes.

File size [latex]=1M=2^{20}=1{,}048{,}576[/latex] bytes. Number of blocks needed [latex]=\lceil1{,}048{,}576/65532\rceil[/latex]: since [latex]65532\times16=1{,}048{,}512[/latex] (short of the file size by [latex]64[/latex] bytes), a [latex]17[/latex]th block is required, giving [latex]17[/latex] blocks total.

Total disk space allocated [latex]=17\times65536=1{,}114{,}112[/latex] bytes. Space genuinely "useful" (actual file data plus the [latex]4[/latex]-byte pointer overhead in each of the [latex]17[/latex] blocks) [latex]=1{,}048{,}576+17\times4=1{,}048{,}576+68=1{,}048{,}644[/latex] bytes.

Internal fragmentation (wasted space) [latex]=1{,}114{,}112-1{,}048{,}644=65{,}468[/latex] bytes.

Answer: 65468

I-2 (counting semaphore = 2): two threads can be inside together and updates can be lost. To get the minimum:
- a decr thread reads X = 10 and is preempted;

- the first decr writes 10 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 9, wiping out all 5 increments;

So [latex]V_2=7[/latex].

questions.question:
Consider a system that has a cache memory unit and a memory management unit (MMU). The address input to the cache memory is a physical address. The MMU has a translation lookaside buffer (TLB). Assume that when a page is evicted from the main memory, the corresponding blocks in the cache are marked as invalid.

For a given memory reference, which of the following sequences of events can NEVER happen?

options.A: TLB miss, Page table hit, Cache hit
options.B: TLB hit, Page table miss, Cache hit
options.C: TLB miss, Page table miss, Cache hit
options.D: TLB miss, Page table miss, Cache miss

questions.explanation:
A memory reference passes through, in order: TLB → (page table, only if TLB misses) → cache.

- TLB miss, Page table hit, Cache hit: possible — TLB doesn't have the mapping, page table does (page is in memory), and the corresponding cache block (whose validity depends on the page being resident) can indeed be valid and hit. Can happen.
- TLB hit, Page table miss, Cache hit: impossible. A TLB hit means the page is currently mapped/resident in memory (TLB entries are only valid for pages currently in memory); it is therefore contradictory for the page table to then report a miss (page not in memory) for that very same page.
- TLB miss, Page table miss, Cache hit: impossible. A page-table miss means the page is not in main memory at all — and the problem states that when a page is evicted, its cache blocks are marked invalid. So if the page isn't in memory, its cache blocks cannot be valid, and a cache hit is impossible.
- TLB miss, Page table miss, Cache miss: possible and in fact the expected/consistent sequence when a page is genuinely not resident.

Answer: "TLB hit, Page table miss, Cache hit" and "TLB miss, Page table miss, Cache hit" can NEVER happen.

questions.question:
The following program consists of 3 concurrent processes and 3 binary semaphores. The semaphores are initialized as S0=1, S1=0, S2=0. How many times will process P0 print '0'?

How many times will process P0 print '0'?
questions.explanation:
P0 prints once (S0 = 1), then releases S1 and S2. P1 and P2 then each release S0 once.

- If both releases happen before P0 waits again, binary S0 stays 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P0 prints once more (2 times).
- If P0 consumes the first release before the second comes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] it prints twice more (3 times).

So it prints at least twice.

Answer: At least twice

questions.question: Consider the following snapshot of a system running n concurrent processes. Process [latex]i[/latex] is holding [latex]X_i[/latex] instances of a resource R, [latex] 1\leq i\leq n[/latex]. Assume that all instances of R are currently in use. Further, for all [latex]i[/latex], process [latex]i[/latex] can place a request for at most [latex]Y_i[/latex] additional instances of R while holding the [latex]X_i[/latex] instances it already has. Of the n processes, there are exactly two processes p and q such that [latex]Y_p=Y_q=0[/latex]. Which one of the following conditions guarantees that no other process apart from p and q can complete execution?
questions.explanation:
p and q need nothing more, so they finish and release [latex]X_p+X_q[/latex] instances (all others are in use).

Any other process k can finish only if it gets [latex]Y_k[/latex] instances. If [latex]X_p+X_q \lt \min_k Y_k[/latex], the freed instances are not enough for any other process, so none of them can complete.

Answer: [latex]X_p+X_q \lt Min\{Y_k\}[/latex]
